summary: A topic guide for separating the decision to recover another guard from the decision to keep attacking from half guard.
description: Use Stephan Kesting’s public half-to-closed-guard discussion to frame a specific half-guard study problem.
overview: Kesting’s article presents leaving half guard as a legitimate choice when that position is being shut down. This page uses that question to organize recovery study and compare focused half-guard resources.

fits: You keep selecting another half-guard attack when your actual question is whether to recover a different guard.
consider_alternative_if: For a source-indexed half-butterfly course companion, compare Brian Glick; for coming up from guard, compare Dante Leon.

includes: A public explanation of why a half-guard player might choose closed-guard recovery.
A study distinction between pursuing offense and changing the starting guard.
limits: This page covers recovery decisions; it does not establish an Andrew Wiltse curriculum or attribute a universal back-take priority to him.

start_here.title: Separate changing guard from abandoning the exchange
start_here.task: Read Kesting’s reason for returning to closed guard. Write down one recent half-guard exchange in which you kept pursuing the same attack. Identify whether your unanswered question is how to attack or how to recover another guard; take that specific question to the relevant instruction rather than assuming a fixed sweep-to-back chain.

flashcards.question: Is staying in half guard always the goal when its attacks are being shut down?
flashcards.answer: No. Kesting’s article discusses recovering closed guard as another choice, rather than repeatedly forcing the same half-guard game.
